body.x: CubicSpace Technologies, Inc. today announced the launch of CubicScreen, a new consumer product designed to unlock the full potential of spatial photos and videos captured on iPhone. Built around proprietary adaptive stereoscopic geometry and glasses-free 3D display technology, CubicScreen allows users to experience their own everyday moments with natural depth and presence, without requiring special eyewear or additional hardware.

CubicScreen transforms iPhone-captured spatial media into vivid personal 3D experiences by combining a thin 3D optical screen protector with an intuitive spatial media application. The company explained that this approach reduces longstanding barriers to 3D viewing and positions smartphones as the most accessible entry point to the expanding spatial media ecosystem. Product availability is planned for the second quarter, with commercial release targeted for Q2 2026, and showcase demonstrations at CES 2026, Eureka Park Booth #60840.

Since Apple introduced spatial photo and video capture capabilities in 2023, hundreds of millions of iPhone owners have gained the ability to record memories in 3D using a device they already carry every day. However, most of that content can still only be viewed in 2D on phones, limiting the emotional connection and immersive impact captured in the original moment. CubicScreen directly addresses this gap by enabling natural and comfortable 3D playback on the same device used for capture, allowing users to relive personal memories exactly as they were intended to be seen.

The CubicScreen app, powered by CubicSpace’s adaptive 3D model, dynamically adjusts 3D geometry in real time based on the content, the individual viewer, and surrounding viewing conditions. The company emphasized that this scientific breakthrough replaces the one-size-fits-all assumptions that traditional stereoscopic displays have relied on for decades. As a result, users receive a guaranteed comfortable and intuitive 3D experience that works consistently in everyday life, requiring no technical expertise or manual adjustments.

Nicholas Routhier, President and Co-Founder of CubicSpace Technologies, described the product as an important milestone for mainstream adoption of 3D. “For the first time in history, hundreds of millions of people can capture their own memories in 3D using a smartphone,” he said. “With CubicScreen, we are removing the friction that has always held 3D back. No glasses, no extra devices, and no expertise required. Our mission is to make 3D as natural and universal as smartphone photography.”

At CES 2026, attendees will be able to experience live demonstrations showing how CubicScreen enables instant 3D playback of personal spatial photos and videos captured on iPhone. Visitors will also discover how the platform fits into a broader ecosystem of glasses-free 3D and XR devices, highlighting opportunities for integration, partnerships, and future content experiences.

CubicSpace Technologies added that its core adaptive stereoscopic geometry technology is protected by a growing intellectual property portfolio that includes four patent families across multiple jurisdictions, with nine patents already granted and nine additional patents currently pending worldwide. The company views this portfolio as a foundation for long-term global expansion and standardization in consumer spatial media.

Founded in 2023, CubicSpace Technologies, Inc. is a deep-tech company specializing in advanced stereoscopic image processing technologies. The company develops adaptive 3D playback solutions designed to deliver natural, comfortable, and intuitive 3D experiences across a wide range of devices and use cases. CubicSpace is headquartered in Montreal, Canada, and is dedicated to making 3D mainstream as part of everyday digital life.
